stem.text: Given \(f(x)=x^{3}+1\), determine the equation of \(f^{-1}(x)\).

extensions.latexSource: Given \(f(x)=x^{3}+1\), determine the equation of \(f^{-1}(x)\).

solution.text:
Let \(y=f(x)\)

\[ y=x^{3}+1 \]

To determine the inverse of \(f(x)\), switch \(x\) and \(y\).

\[ \begin{aligned}  x=y^{3}+1 \\  x-1=y^{3} \\  \sqrt[3]{x-1}=y \\  f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt[3]{x-1} \end{aligned} \]

1 mark for switching \(x\) and \(y\)

\(\frac{1}{2}\) mark for isolating \(y\)

\(\frac{1}{2}\) mark for writing equation in terms of \(f^{-1}(x)\)

2 marks

stem.text: Justify whether \(\frac{5 \pi}{8}\) and \(-\frac{11 \pi}{4}\) are coterminal angles.

extensions.latexSource: Justify whether \(\frac{5 \pi}{8}\) and \(-\frac{11 \pi}{4}\) are coterminal angles.

solution.text:
Method 1

\[ \begin{aligned}  \frac{5 \pi}{8}-\left(-\frac{11 \pi}{4}\right) \\  \frac{5 \pi}{8}+\frac{11 \pi}{4} \\  \frac{5 \pi}{8}+\frac{22 \pi}{8} \\  \frac{27 \pi}{8} \end{aligned} \]

Since \(\frac{27 \pi}{8}\) is not a multiple of \(2 \pi\) they are not coterminal angles.

1 mark

Method 2

Coterminal angles of \(\frac{5 \pi}{8}\) :

\[ \begin{aligned}  \frac{5 \pi}{8}-\frac{16 \pi}{8}=-\frac{11 \pi}{8} \\  -\frac{11 \pi}{8}-\frac{16 \pi}{8}=-\frac{27 \pi}{8} \end{aligned} \]

Coterminal angles of \(-\frac{11 \pi}{4}\) :

\[ -\frac{11 \pi}{4}\left(\frac{2}{2}\right)=-\frac{22 \pi}{8} \]

∴ Angles are not coterminal since \(-\frac{27 \pi}{8} \neq-\frac{22 \pi}{8}\).

1 mark

stem.text:
Suzanne was asked to determine the value of \(\tan \theta\), given that \(\sec \theta=-\frac{8}{3}\) and \(\theta\) terminates in

quadrant II.

Describe her error.
